   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "45fd39e4",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "# A quick introduction to mpstab\n",
    "\n",
    "mpstab simulates quantum circuits with a *hybrid stabilizer-MPS* representation: the Clifford part of a circuit is handled by a fast stabilizer simulator, and only the non-Clifford (\"magic\") gates are pushed into a matrix product state (MPS). In this tutorial you will learn how to wrap a qibo circuit in an `HSMPO` surrogate, compute expectation values, check them against an exact simulation, and see why magic gates, not qubits, set the cost of a simulation."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "b1c16660",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Setup\n",
    "\n",
    "We build circuits with [qibo](https://qibo.science) and simulate them with mpstab's `HSMPO` class. We also load the shared plot style used by all mpstab tutorials."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 1,
   "id": "857b648f",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-11-18T14:42:18.336274Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-11-18T14:42:18.336108Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-11-18T14:42:23.192274Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-11-18T14:42:23.191531Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "import sys\n",
    "import time\n",
    "\n",
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "import numpy as np\n",
    "from qibo import Circuit, gates, hamiltonians, set_backend\n",
    "from qibo.symbols import X, Z\n",
    "\n",
    "from mpstab import HSMPO, pauli_string_to_hamiltonian\n",
    "from mpstab.models.ansatze import HardwareEfficient\n",
    "sys.path.append(\"../..\")  # examples/, home of the plot style\n",
    "from plotting import COLORS, set_style\n",
    "\n",
    "set_backend(\"numpy\")  # qibo's exact statevector simulator, used as a reference\n",
    "set_style()\n",
    "np.random.seed(42)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "dd232f64",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## A first circuit\n",
    "\n",
    "We prepare a GHZ-like entangled state with Hadamard and CNOT gates, then add a layer of $R_Y(\\theta)$ rotations and a chain of CZ gates. The rotations are the only non-Clifford gates. Passing the circuit to `HSMPO` splits it into its Clifford and magic parts and builds the MPS once."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 2,
   "id": "aa70187e",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-11-18T14:42:23.194439Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-11-18T14:42:23.194145Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-11-18T14:42:23.203475Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-11-18T14:42:23.202948Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "0: ─H─o─────────RY─o─────────\n",
      "1: ───X─o───────RY─Z─o───────\n",
      "2: ─────X─o─────RY───Z─o─────\n",
      "3: ───────X─o───RY─────Z─o───\n",
      "4: ─────────X─o─RY───────Z─o─\n",
      "5: ───────────X─RY─────────Z─\n",
      "Clifford gates: 11, magic gates: 6\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "nqubits = 6\n",
    "\n",
    "def build_circuit(theta):\n",
    "    circuit = Circuit(nqubits)\n",
    "    circuit.add(gates.H(0))\n",
    "    for q in range(nqubits - 1):\n",
    "        circuit.add(gates.CNOT(q, q + 1))\n",
    "    for q in range(nqubits):\n",
    "        circuit.add(gates.RY(q, theta=theta))\n",
    "    for q in range(nqubits - 1):\n",
    "        circuit.add(gates.CZ(q, q + 1))\n",
    "    return circuit\n",
    "\n",
    "circuit = build_circuit(theta=0.3)\n",
    "circuit.draw()\n",
    "\n",
    "surrogate = HSMPO(circuit, progress=False)\n",
    "print(f\"Clifford gates: {surrogate.n_clifford_gates}, magic gates: {surrogate.n_magic_gates}\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "fc8db86d",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Expectation values\n",
    "\n",
    "`expectation` takes a Pauli string, with qubit 0 as the leftmost character. For observables made of several terms you can pass a `{pauli_string: coefficient}` dictionary or a qibo `SymbolicHamiltonian`. Here we measure the correlator $Z_0 Z_5$ and the energy of a transverse-field Ising chain, $H = \\sum_i Z_i Z_{i+1} + \\tfrac12 \\sum_i X_i$."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 3,
   "id": "3b3eb43c",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-11-18T14:42:23.206128Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-11-18T14:42:23.205946Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-11-18T14:42:23.215238Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-11-18T14:42:23.214644Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "<Z0 Z5>          = 0.912668\n",
      "<H_Ising>        = 4.845660\n",
      "<Z0Z1 + 0.5 X0>  = 1.053828\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "zz = surrogate.expectation(\"ZIIIIZ\")\n",
    "\n",
    "ising = hamiltonians.SymbolicHamiltonian(\n",
    "    sum(Z(i) * Z(i + 1) for i in range(nqubits - 1)) + 0.5 * sum(X(i) for i in range(nqubits))\n",
    ")\n",
    "energy = surrogate.expectation(ising)\n",
    "\n",
    "two_terms = surrogate.expectation({\"ZZIIII\": 1.0, \"XIIIII\": 0.5})\n",
    "\n",
    "print(f\"<Z0 Z5>          = {zz:.6f}\")\n",
    "print(f\"<H_Ising>        = {energy:.6f}\")\n",
    "print(f\"<Z0Z1 + 0.5 X0>  = {two_terms:.6f}\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "915a274a",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Checking against the exact state\n",
    "\n",
    "On a few qubits we can compare with qibo's exact statevector. `pauli_string_to_hamiltonian` turns a Pauli string into a qibo Hamiltonian. Without a bond-dimension cap the hybrid representation is exact, so the two numbers agree to machine precision."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 4,
   "id": "97d572f9",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-11-18T14:42:23.218012Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-11-18T14:42:23.217852Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-11-18T14:42:23.226957Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-11-18T14:42:23.226423Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "<Z0 Z5>   mpstab = 0.9126678075   exact = 0.9126678075\n",
      "<H_Ising> mpstab = 4.8456602740   exact = 4.8456602740\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "state = circuit().state()\n",
    "exact_zz = pauli_string_to_hamiltonian(\"ZIIIIZ\").expectation_from_state(state)\n",
    "exact_energy = ising.expectation_from_state(state)\n",
    "\n",
    "print(f\"<Z0 Z5>   mpstab = {zz:.10f}   exact = {exact_zz:.10f}\")\n",
    "print(f\"<H_Ising> mpstab = {energy:.10f}   exact = {exact_energy:.10f}\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "8f46679f",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### Sweeping a rotation angle\n",
    "\n",
    "Circuit parameters can be updated in place with `set_parameters`, which rebuilds the MPS. Let's sweep $\\theta$ and follow the Ising energy. At multiples of $\\pi/2$ the rotations become Clifford gates, so the number of magic gates drops to zero."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 5,
   "id": "7df7ec29",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-11-18T14:42:23.229056Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-11-18T14:42:23.228891Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-11-18T14:42:23.508263Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-11-18T14:42:23.507354Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "magic gates along the sweep: [0, 6, 6, 6, 6, 6, 0, 6, 6, 6, 6, 6, 0]\n"
     ]
    },
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 880x550 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "thetas = np.linspace(0, np.pi, 13)\n",
    "mpstab_energy, exact_energy, n_magic = [], [], []\n",
    "for theta in thetas:\n",
    "    surrogate.set_parameters([theta] * nqubits)\n",
    "    mpstab_energy.append(surrogate.expectation(ising))\n",
    "    n_magic.append(surrogate.n_magic_gates)\n",
    "    exact_energy.append(ising.expectation_from_state(build_circuit(theta)().state()))\n",
    "\n",
    "print(\"magic gates along the sweep:\", n_magic)\n",
    "\n",
    "plt.plot(thetas, mpstab_energy, \"o\", label=\"mpstab\")\n",
    "plt.plot(thetas, exact_energy, \"--\", color=COLORS[\"gray\"], label=\"exact (qibo)\")\n",
    "plt.xlabel(r\"rotation angle $\\theta$\")\n",
    "plt.ylabel(r\"$\\langle H_\\mathrm{Ising} \\rangle$\")\n",
    "plt.title(\"mpstab matches the exact statevector\")\n",
    "plt.legend()\n",
    "plt.show()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "4c35ee7c",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Clifford circuits are free\n",
    "\n",
    "A circuit made only of Clifford gates never touches the MPS: it is simulated by the stabilizer engine alone, in polynomial time. This lets us prepare a 1000-qubit GHZ state and measure global observables in a fraction of a second, far beyond any statevector simulator."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 6,
   "id": "a616cfef",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-11-18T14:42:23.510974Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-11-18T14:42:23.510737Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-11-18T14:42:23.786902Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-11-18T14:42:23.785984Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "magic gates: 0\n",
      "<Z...Z> = 1.000\n",
      "<X...X> = 1.000\n",
      "<Z0>    = 0.000\n",
      "elapsed: 0.12 s\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "n_ghz = 1000\n",
    "ghz = Circuit(n_ghz)\n",
    "ghz.add(gates.H(0))\n",
    "for q in range(n_ghz - 1):\n",
    "    ghz.add(gates.CNOT(q, q + 1))\n",
    "\n",
    "start = time.time()\n",
    "ghz_surrogate = HSMPO(ghz, progress=False)\n",
    "print(f\"magic gates: {ghz_surrogate.n_magic_gates}\")\n",
    "print(f\"<Z...Z> = {ghz_surrogate.expectation('Z' * n_ghz):.3f}\")\n",
    "print(f\"<X...X> = {ghz_surrogate.expectation('X' * n_ghz):.3f}\")\n",
    "print(f\"<Z0>    = {ghz_surrogate.expectation('Z' + 'I' * (n_ghz - 1)):.3f}\")\n",
    "print(f\"elapsed: {time.time() - start:.2f} s\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "68772806",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Magic gates are what costs\n",
    "\n",
    "Every magic gate becomes a Pauli rotation applied to the MPS, and each one can grow its bond dimension. A ready-made ansatz from `mpstab.models.ansatze` makes this easy to see: `HardwareEfficient` stacks layers of random $R_Y$ rotations (all magic) and rings of CZ gates (Clifford). Without a cap, the bond dimension of the MPS grows with the number of layers."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 7,
   "id": "d24cd9e3",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-11-18T14:42:23.789961Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-11-18T14:42:23.789715Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-11-18T14:42:23.944784Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-11-18T14:42:23.943934Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "layers = 1: magic gates =  12, bond dimension = 1\n",
      "layers = 2: magic gates =  24, bond dimension = 16\n",
      "layers = 4: magic gates =  48, bond dimension = 54\n"
     ]
    },
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "layers = 6: magic gates =  72, bond dimension = 64\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "n_he = 12\n",
    "for nlayers in [1, 2, 4, 6]:\n",
    "    ansatz = HardwareEfficient(nqubits=n_he, nlayers=nlayers)\n",
    "    hs = HSMPO(ansatz, progress=False)\n",
    "    print(f\"layers = {nlayers}: magic gates = {hs.n_magic_gates:3d}, \"\n",
    "          f\"bond dimension = {hs.original_circuit_mps.max_bond()}\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "5d2fb206",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### Trading accuracy for speed\n",
    "\n",
    "For larger circuits we cap the MPS with `max_bond_dimension`. Truncation loses some of the state, and `return_fidelity=True` reports how much: the squared norm of the truncated MPS, which is 1 when nothing was discarded. Deeper circuits carry more magic and need a larger bond dimension to reach the same fidelity."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 8,
   "id": "10df39d0",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-11-18T14:42:23.948671Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-11-18T14:42:23.948394Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-11-18T14:42:24.426933Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-11-18T14:42:24.426195Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 880x550 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "bond_dims = [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64]\n",
    "for nlayers, marker in [(2, \"o\"), (6, \"s\")]:\n",
    "    ansatz = HardwareEfficient(nqubits=n_he, nlayers=nlayers)\n",
    "    fidelities = []\n",
    "    for chi in bond_dims:\n",
    "        hs = HSMPO(ansatz, max_bond_dimension=chi, progress=False)\n",
    "        _, fidelity = hs.expectation(\"Z\" * n_he, return_fidelity=True)\n",
    "        fidelities.append(abs(fidelity))\n",
    "    plt.plot(bond_dims, fidelities, marker + \"-\", label=f\"{nlayers} layers ({hs.n_magic_gates} magic gates)\")\n",
    "\n",
    "plt.axhline(1, ls=\":\", color=COLORS[\"gray\"])\n",
    "plt.xscale(\"log\", base=2)\n",
    "plt.xticks(bond_dims, bond_dims)\n",
    "plt.xlabel(\"max bond dimension\")\n",
    "plt.ylabel(\"truncation fidelity\")\n",
    "plt.title(f\"More magic needs a larger bond dimension ({n_he} qubits)\")\n",
    "plt.legend()\n",
    "plt.show()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "ec6f4295",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "The fidelity also tells you how far to trust a truncated result. Let's compare the Ising energy of the 6-layer circuit at a few bond dimensions with the exact value. Since a surrogate without a cap is exact, as we checked above, we use it as the reference."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 9,
   "id": "69a25cb8",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-11-18T14:42:24.429043Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-11-18T14:42:24.428875Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-11-18T14:42:24.657493Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-11-18T14:42:24.656806Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "exact energy: 0.522727\n",
      "chi =  4: energy = 0.643416, |error| = 1.2e-01, fidelity = 0.5284\n",
      "chi = 16: energy = 0.523519, |error| = 7.9e-04, fidelity = 0.9878\n",
      "chi = 64: energy = 0.522727, |error| = 0.0e+00, fidelity = 1.0000\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "ising_he = hamiltonians.SymbolicHamiltonian(\n",
    "    sum(Z(i) * Z(i + 1) for i in range(n_he - 1)) + 0.5 * sum(X(i) for i in range(n_he))\n",
    ")\n",
    "exact = HSMPO(ansatz, progress=False).expectation(ising_he)\n",
    "print(f\"exact energy: {exact:.6f}\")\n",
    "for chi in [4, 16, 64]:\n",
    "    hs = HSMPO(ansatz, max_bond_dimension=chi, progress=False)\n",
    "    value, fidelity = hs.expectation(ising_he, return_fidelity=True)\n",
    "    print(f\"chi = {chi:2d}: energy = {value:.6f}, |error| = {abs(value - exact):.1e}, fidelity = {abs(fidelity):.4f}\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "9dbcbf00",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Where to go next\n",
    "\n",
    "You now know the core workflow: build a circuit, wrap it in `HSMPO`, and call `expectation`. The other tutorials build on it:\n",
    "\n",
    "- **Pauli noise simulation**: noisy circuits with Pauli and coherent errors and readout errors.\n",
    "- **Non-unital noise simulation**: relaxation and other Kraus channels, crosstalk, idle noise, preparation and asymmetric readout errors.\n",
    "- **Data-driven error mitigation**: CDR and vnCDR, learning the noise from near-Clifford circuits that mpstab simulates cheaply.\n",
    "- **Ground states with DMRG**: optimizing an MPS starting from an `HSMPO` surrogate to find ground-state energies.\n",
    "- **State metrics**: measuring entanglement and magic of the states mpstab prepares."
   ]
  }
 ],
